claims.text: The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide taught how to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, import and use Terraform modules directly, convert HCL to Pulumi, and orchestrate Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.
Any Terraform provider can be used in Pulumi programs.
Terraform modules can be imported and used directly in Pulumi.
The Pulumi `terraform.state.S3Reference` class exists (in `@pulumi/terraform`) and takes `bucket` and `key` arguments to reference Terraform state in S3, with a `getOutput` method.
`terraform.state.S3Reference` is accessible as `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` from the `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` import.
`new pulumi.StackReference("core-infra")` with `getOutput("vpcId")` retrieves outputs from another Pulumi stack.
`pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.

The `pulumi import` command takes arguments in the form `<type> <name> <id>`, e.g. `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`, and the type tokens `aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc`, `aws:ec2/subnet:Subnet`, `aws:ecs/cluster:Cluster` are valid.
State ownership can be transferred gradually, resource-by-resource, from Terraform to Pulumi.
`getOutput("resources")` on a Terraform state reference returns a list of state resources that can be filtered by `type`.
Pulumi has an import API that can be used programmatically to import resources.
Pulumi policies can enforce infrastructure policies across both Terraform and Pulumi resources.
`@pulumi/policy` exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`; policies use `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"` and `validateResource` with a `(resource, args, reportViolation)` callback.
The `aws.s3.Bucket` resource has an `acl` property that can equal "public-read" or "public-read-write".
`aws.ecs.Cluster` accepts `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` with `kmsKeyId` and `logging: "DEFAULT"`.
The Automation API `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` takes `stackName`, `projectName`, and `program`; `stack.setConfig` and `stack.up({onOutput})` exist and `up` result has `outputs`.
The Automation API lets you embed Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.

Component resources can wrap Terraform-managed infrastructure so developers can create WebApplications in Pulumi without knowing they depend on Terraform-managed resources, leaving multi-tool complexity to platform teams.

`aws.lb.LoadBalancer`, `aws.ecs.TaskDefinition` (with `requiresCompatibilities`, `networkMode: awsvpc`, cpu "256", memory "512") and `aws.ecs.Service` (with `launchType: FARGATE`, `networkConfiguration.assignPublicIp`) accept the arguments used in the example.
